content_html:
What if the Higgs boson found in 2012 is not alone but is the only sibling we have encountered so far? Scientists at CERN discovered the particle that year, and it was a major discovery because it explained how other particles acquire mass. For a long time, scientists thought this was the final piece of the puzzle.

They have a framework called the Standard Model that describes the smallest particles in everything we see. This includes electrons in atoms and light particles called photons. However, this framework does not explain everything. It does not tell us about dark matter or why the universe has so much more matter than antimatter. It is like having a map that shows only half the world.

The discovery of the Higgs boson created new questions. Many physicists started wondering whether the Higgs we found is the only one of its kind. They began to ask whether there is a larger family of these particles hiding in the universe. If we find more members of this family, we might finally understand the parts of nature that the current framework misses.

A three-Higgs proposal

This idea is the focus of two recent studies by researchers from IIT Gandhinagar. They worked with experts from Harish-Chandra Research Institute (HRI) to explore a theory in which there are three types of these fields instead of just one.

The team at IIT Gandhinagar included Akshat Khanna, who has a Ph.D. in physics; Baradhwaj Coleppa, associate professor of physics; Nipun Batra, associate professor of computer science and engineering; and Gokul B. Krishna, who has a Ph.D. in physics. They published their findings and shared their work at an international conference, PASCOS, at Durham University.

Their first study, published in Physical Review D, used a machine learning method called active learning to sort through thousands of possibilities, laying the foundation.

The second study, published in The European Physical Journal, looked at how a future particle collider could detect these new family members. Together, the papers provide a better map for future science experiments.

How the fields divide the work

To understand their work, think of the Higgs field as a basic building block of the universe. In the standard framework, there is only one of these blocks. As the universe evolved, interactions with this field gave mass to all the particles that make up everything around us. This leaves behind one Higgs particle.

The new theory suggests there are three different building blocks. This means there would be several new types of particles. Some might have electric charges, and others might behave in ways we have never seen before.

Each block also carries a background value—the strength of the field even in empty space—and, with three blocks instead of one, the fields can mix with one another. The result is a much richer collection of Higgs particles, including charged Higgs bosons that do not exist in the Standard Model and are now being sought in experiments.

This specific model is often called a democratic theory because the three building blocks share the work of giving mass to different kinds of matter. One block takes care of particles like electrons. Another block handles a specific set of quarks, and the third block looks after another set.

If these building blocks all interacted freely with the same kinds of matter, they might cause strange reactions that have never been seen in experiments. By giving each block a specific job, the theory stays consistent with what we already know to be true.

Fitting the known Higgs in

One important idea in the study is deciding which of the new particles is the one we already found. Since we know the mass of the current Higgs boson, we have to fit it into the new family. It could be the lightest member, or it could be the middle member.

It could even be the heaviest member. These different arrangements change how the rest of the family looks. The researchers looked at each of these scenarios to see which ones make the most sense according to the latest scientific data.

Every set of parameters in the model must pass several strict tests before it is considered valid. The energy of the system must stay stable so it does not collapse. The predictions must also match data from past experiments at particle colliders.

Most importantly, the Higgs particle we already discovered must still look and act the same way it does in our observations. The new particles cannot interfere with laws of physics that we have already proven to be correct. This keeps the theory grounded in reality.

Coleppa explains, "A plethora of theoretical possibilities remain in which this model could be consistent with experimental observations. Our task is to test these possibilities in the most general and comprehensive way."

Teaching the search where to dig

Here is where the size of the problem becomes almost comical. Imagine a board game with 14 different dials, with every dial turned to a different setting. Flip just one dial on or off, and you already have 214, or more than 16,000 combinations.

But these dials are not simple on-off switches; each one can be set to any value within a range, like a volume knob rather than a light switch. To map out this game properly, the team generated 600 billion random combinations of mass and angle settings and tested each one against the rules.

Out of those 600 billion attempts, only a tiny sliver survived all the tests. Checking each one by traditional methods, one at a time, would be like trying every possible combination on a bank vault by hand.

Picture this entire 14-dial search space as a vast, foggy beach, with a few important coins buried somewhere in the sand. A metal detector that beeps everywhere would be useless; you would dig forever. The trick the researchers used, called active learning, is closer to a smarter detector that learns from where it has already dug. It starts small, digging in a handful of random spots and keeping track of which ones turn up coins.

After a few rounds, it stops digging at random altogether. It starts noticing a rough line in the sand: On one side, coins keep showing up; on the other, nothing. Right along that line is where it keeps getting surprised.

So that is where it digs next, again and again, each new hole sharpening its sense of exactly where that line runs, until it has a confident map of the whole boundary without ever touching most of the beach. As one final safety check, anything it flagged as promising was dug up by hand anyway, just to make sure it was not a false alarm.

The result of swapping blind digging for this smarter search was dramatic: An analysis that used to take about four hours could now be done in around 10 minutes, with no real particles missed along the way.

Batra explains, "Not every data point is equally informative for training a machine learning model. Active learning addresses this by selecting a small but highly informative subset of data, enabling the model to learn more efficiently."

Three possible family trees

With the search done, the team had a clear map, and it turned out the family of three Higgs bosons can be arranged in three different ways, depending on whether the 125 GeV Higgs we already know is the youngest, middle or oldest sibling.

In the first arrangement, our known Higgs is the youngest, the lightest of the three. Here, the model is well-behaved. Its two heavier siblings are predicted to weigh somewhere between roughly 350 and 580 GeV, several times heavier than the Higgs we have already found.

Nature, it seems, is allowed to have bigger siblings hiding just out of reach of past experiments, but not absolutely any weight will do; they have to fall inside this specific window.

The most interesting twist comes from the second arrangement, where our known Higgs is the middle child. This setup quietly allows for something remarkable: a second, lighter Higgs boson, possibly as light as 82 GeV, that nobody has detected yet.

It is not that this particle would have been invisible; it is that it may interact with other particles differently enough to have hidden in plain sight within data we already have. That is the headline result of the whole study. A sibling of the Higgs boson, lighter than the one history books already credited with completing the Standard Model, remains entirely on the table.

The third arrangement is the one nature seems to veto. Here, our known Higgs would have to be the oldest, the heaviest of the three, which would mean two undiscovered Higgs bosons lighter than 125 GeV are floating around. On paper, this sounds just as exciting as the middle-child case. But when the team pushed this scenario through the full gauntlet of tests, it failed.

A cleaner machine for the hunt

The second paper looks at how we can actually find these hidden particles. The researchers focused on a proposed machine called the International Linear Collider. This machine would collide tiny particles to create a very clean environment for study. It is different from the machines we use today because it allows scientists to see the results of collisions much more clearly.

The team investigated several ways this future machine could produce the new Higgs family members in a laboratory setting.

The researchers found several promising ways to spot the new particles. When the machine collides particles, it can create pairs of the new Higgs family. These particles quickly break down into other things that we can see and measure. By counting these final pieces, scientists can separate the real signal from the background noise.

This is similar to listening for a specific voice in a crowded room. If you know what to listen for, you can find the information you need even when there is a lot of other sound.

The study shows that many of these paths could lead to a real discovery. Some channels are very likely to show results if the machine runs for a certain amount of time. The researchers looked at different types of signals, including those that produce specific patterns of quarks and leptons.

This provides a clear set of instructions for future experiments. It turns the theoretical map into a practical guide for the scientists who build and run these massive machines.

From theory to a test plan

The strength of this work is how it connects theory with experiment. The first study uses smart computers to find the best possibilities, and the second study tells us how to look for them. This is very important because theories with too many options can be hard to test.

The researchers at IIT Gandhinagar made their theory testable by narrowing down the search. As the team explains, combining physics with smart computer strategies allows us to search for the secrets of the universe much faster than before.

This research is about more than just one theory. It helps the global effort to see whether the Higgs boson is alone or has siblings. It also proves that smart computer tools can help scientists navigate very complex problems.

This method can be used in many other areas of science where there are too many possibilities to test. The immediate goal is to help find new particles, but the long-term goal is to improve how we do science in a world with so much information.

The story of the Higgs boson is really a story about how the universe is built. We started with one particle, but we might have a much bigger family. The studies at IIT Gandhinagar show that this idea is very much alive.

One lighter sibling might be hiding in our current data, while others might be waiting for future machines. By using smart computers to draw the map and collider studies to lead the way, we are getting closer to understanding the full architecture of our world.

Khanna adds, "The key to our work was using innovative ways like combining modern ML techniques with particle physics to tackle a formidable challenge. In the near future, I am eager to pursue this line of research even further, in search of evidence of new particles."

sentences.en: In the standard framework, there is only one of these blocks.
sentences.zh: 在标准框架中，只有这些块之一。

sentences.en: As the universe evolved, interactions with this field gave mass to all the particles that make up everything around us.
sentences.zh: 随着宇宙的演化，与这个场的相互作用为构成我们周围一切的所有粒子提供了质量。

sentences.en: This leaves behind one Higgs particle.
sentences.zh: 这留下了一个希格斯粒子。

blocks.html_en: The new theory suggests there are three different building blocks. This means there would be several new types of particles. Some might have electric charges, and others might behave in ways we have never seen before.

sentences.en: The new theory suggests there are three different building blocks.
sentences.zh: 新理论表明存在三种不同的构建模块。

sentences.en: This means there would be several new types of particles.
sentences.zh: 这意味着将会出现几种新型粒子。

sentences.en: Some might have electric charges, and others might behave in ways we have never seen before.
sentences.zh: 有些可能带有电荷，而另一些可能会以我们以前从未见过的方式表现。

blocks.html_en: Each block also carries a background value—the strength of the field even in empty space—and, with three blocks instead of one, the fields can mix with one another. The result is a much richer collection of Higgs particles, including charged Higgs bosons that do not exist in the Standard Model and are now being sought in experiments.

sentences.en: Each block also carries a background value—the strength of the field even in empty space—and, with three blocks instead of one, the fields can mix with one another.
sentences.zh: 每个块还带有一个背景值——即使在空白空间中的场强度——并且，用三个块而不是一个，场可以彼此混合。

sentences.en: The result is a much richer collection of Higgs particles, including charged Higgs bosons that do not exist in the Standard Model and are now being sought in experiments.
sentences.zh: 其结果是希格斯粒子的集合更加丰富，包括标准模型中不存在的带电希格斯玻色子，现在正在实验中寻找。

blocks.html_en: This specific model is often called a democratic theory because the three building blocks share the work of giving mass to different kinds of matter. One block takes care of particles like electrons. Another block handles a specific set of quarks, and the third block looks after another set.

sentences.en: This specific model is often called a democratic theory because the three building blocks share the work of giving mass to different kinds of matter.
sentences.zh: 这种特定的模型通常被称为民主理论，因为这三个构建模块共同承担为不同种类的物质提供质量的工作。

sentences.en: One block takes care of particles like electrons.
sentences.zh: 其中一个模块负责处理电子等粒子。

sentences.en: Another block handles a specific set of quarks, and the third block looks after another set.
sentences.zh: 另一个块处理一组特定的夸克，第三个块处理另一组夸克。

blocks.html_en: If these building blocks all interacted freely with the same kinds of matter, they might cause strange reactions that have never been seen in experiments. By giving each block a specific job, the theory stays consistent with what we already know to be true.

sentences.en: If these building blocks all interacted freely with the same kinds of matter, they might cause strange reactions that have never been seen in experiments.
sentences.zh: 如果这些构建块都与相同种类的物质自由相互作用，它们可能会引起实验中从未见过的奇怪反应。

sentences.en: By giving each block a specific job, the theory stays consistent with what we already know to be true.
sentences.zh: 通过为每个块分配特定的工作，该理论与我们已知的事实保持一致。

blocks.html_en: Fitting the known Higgs in

sentences.en: Fitting the known Higgs in
sentences.zh: 将已知的希格斯粒子拟合进去

blocks.html_en: One important idea in the study is deciding which of the new particles is the one we already found. Since we know the mass of the current Higgs boson, we have to fit it into the new family. It could be the lightest member, or it could be the middle member.

sentences.en: One important idea in the study is deciding which of the new particles is the one we already found.
sentences.zh: 这项研究中的一个重要想法是确定哪些新粒子是我们已经发现的粒子。

sentences.en: Since we know the mass of the current Higgs boson, we have to fit it into the new family.
sentences.zh: 由于我们知道当前希格斯玻色子的质量，因此我们必须将其放入新的家族中。

sentences.en: It could be the lightest member, or it could be the middle member.
sentences.zh: 它可以是最轻的构件，也可以是中间的构件。

blocks.html_en: It could even be the heaviest member. These different arrangements change how the rest of the family looks. The researchers looked at each of these scenarios to see which ones make the most sense according to the latest scientific data.

sentences.en: It could even be the heaviest member.
sentences.zh: 它甚至可能是最重的成员。

sentences.en: These different arrangements change how the rest of the family looks.
sentences.zh: 这些不同的安排改变了家庭其他成员的外观。

sentences.en: The researchers looked at each of these scenarios to see which ones make the most sense according to the latest scientific data.
sentences.zh: 研究人员根据最新的科学数据对这些场景进行了研究，看看哪些场景最有意义。

blocks.html_en: Every set of parameters in the model must pass several strict tests before it is considered valid. The energy of the system must stay stable so it does not collapse. The predictions must also match data from past experiments at particle colliders.

sentences.en: Every set of parameters in the model must pass several strict tests before it is considered valid.
sentences.zh: 模型中的每组参数都必须经过多次严格的测试才被认为有效。

sentences.en: The energy of the system must stay stable so it does not collapse.
sentences.zh: 系统的能量必须保持稳定，这样才不会崩溃。

sentences.en: The predictions must also match data from past experiments at particle colliders.
sentences.zh: 这些预测还必须与过去粒子对撞机实验的数据相匹配。

blocks.html_en: Most importantly, the Higgs particle we already discovered must still look and act the same way it does in our observations. The new particles cannot interfere with laws of physics that we have already proven to be correct. This keeps the theory grounded in reality.

sentences.en: Most importantly, the Higgs particle we already discovered must still look and act the same way it does in our observations.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，我们已经发现的希格斯粒子的外观和行为必须仍然与我们观察到的相同。

sentences.en: The new particles cannot interfere with laws of physics that we have already proven to be correct.
sentences.zh: 新粒子不会干扰我们已经证明是正确的物理定律。

sentences.en: This keeps the theory grounded in reality.
sentences.zh: 这使得理论立足于现实。

blocks.html_en: Coleppa explains, "A plethora of theoretical possibilities remain in which this model could be consistent with experimental observations. Our task is to test these possibilities in the most general and comprehensive way."

sentences.en: Our task is to test these possibilities in the most general and comprehensive way."
sentences.zh: 我们的任务是以最普遍、最全面的方式测试这些可能性。”

blocks.html_en: Here is where the size of the problem becomes almost comical. Imagine a board game with 14 different dials, with every dial turned to a different setting. Flip just one dial on or off, and you already have 214, or more than 16,000 combinations.

sentences.en: Here is where the size of the problem becomes almost comical.
sentences.zh: 这就是问题的规模变得近乎滑稽的地方。

sentences.en: Imagine a board game with 14 different dials, with every dial turned to a different setting.
sentences.zh: 想象一下有 14 个不同转盘的棋盘游戏，每个转盘都有不同的设置。

sentences.en: Flip just one dial on or off, and you already have 214, or more than 16,000 combinations.
sentences.zh: 只需打开或关闭一个拨盘，您就已经拥有 214 种或超过 16,000 种组合。

blocks.html_en: But these dials are not simple on-off switches; each one can be set to any value within a range, like a volume knob rather than a light switch. sentences.en: But these dials are not simple on-off switches; each one can be set to any value within a range, like a volume knob rather than a light switch.
sentences.zh: 但这些转盘并不是简单的开关；它们是一个简单的开关。每个都可以设置为一定范围内的任何值，就像音量旋钮而不是灯开关。

sentences.en: To map out this game properly, the team generated 600 billion random combinations of mass and angle settings and tested each one against the rules.
sentences.zh: 为了正确地设计这个游戏，团队生成了 6000 亿个质量和角度设置的随机组合，并根据规则测试了每一个组合。

blocks.html_en: Out of those 600 billion attempts, only a tiny sliver survived all the tests. Checking each one by traditional methods, one at a time, would be like trying every possible combination on a bank vault by hand.

sentences.en: Out of those 600 billion attempts, only a tiny sliver survived all the tests.
sentences.zh: 在这 6000 亿次尝试中，只有一小部分能够通过所有测试。

sentences.en: Checking each one by traditional methods, one at a time, would be like trying every possible combination on a bank vault by hand.
sentences.zh: 用传统方法一次检查每一项，就像在银行金库中手工尝试每一种可能的组合一样。

blocks.html_en: Picture this entire 14-dial search space as a vast, foggy beach, with a few important coins buried somewhere in the sand. A metal detector that beeps everywhere would be useless; you would dig forever. The trick the researchers used, called active learning, is closer to a smarter detector that learns from where it has already dug. It starts small, digging in a handful of random spots and keeping track of which ones turn up coins.

sentences.en: Picture this entire 14-dial search space as a vast, foggy beach, with a few important coins buried somewhere in the sand.
sentences.zh: 将整个 14 转盘搜索空间想象成一片广阔、雾气弥漫的海滩，沙子里埋着一些重要的硬币。

sentences.en: A metal detector that beeps everywhere would be useless; you would dig forever.
sentences.zh: 到处发出蜂鸣声的金属探测器是没有用的；你会永远挖下去。

sentences.en: The trick the researchers used, called active learning, is closer to a smarter detector that learns from where it has already dug.
sentences.zh: 研究人员使用的技巧称为主动学习，更接近于从已经挖掘的位置进行学习的更智能的探测器。

sentences.en: It starts small, digging in a handful of random spots and keeping track of which ones turn up coins.
sentences.zh: 它从小处开始，挖掘一些随机点并跟踪哪些点出现了硬币。

blocks.html_en: After a few rounds, it stops digging at random altogether. It starts noticing a rough line in the sand: On one side, coins keep showing up; on the other, nothing. Right along that line is where it keeps getting surprised.

sentences.en: After a few rounds, it stops digging at random altogether.
sentences.zh: 几轮后，它完全停止随机挖掘。

sentences.en: It starts noticing a rough line in the sand: On one side, coins keep showing up; on the other, nothing.
sentences.zh: 它开始注意到沙子上有一条粗糙的线：一侧，硬币不断出现；另一侧，硬币不断出现；另一侧，硬币不断出现。另一方面，什么也没有。

sentences.en: Right along that line is where it keeps getting surprised.
sentences.zh: 沿着这条线就是它不断令人惊讶的地方。

blocks.html_en: So that is where it digs next, again and again, each new hole sharpening its sense of exactly where that line runs, until it has a confident map of the whole boundary without ever touching most of the beach. As one final safety check, anything it flagged as promising was dug up by hand anyway, just to make sure it was not a false alarm.

sentences.en: So that is where it digs next, again and again, each new hole sharpening its sense of exactly where that line runs, until it has a confident map of the whole boundary without ever touching most of the beach.
sentences.zh: 因此，这就是它下一步挖掘的地方，一次又一次，每个新洞都会增强它对这条线的确切位置的感觉，直到它在不触及大部分海滩的情况下拥有整个边界的自信地图。

sentences.en: As one final safety check, anything it flagged as promising was dug up by hand anyway, just to make sure it was not a false alarm.
sentences.zh: 作为最后的安全检查，任何被标记为有希望的东西都会被手工挖掘出来，只是为了确保这不是一场虚惊。

blocks.html_en: The result of swapping blind digging for this smarter search was dramatic: An analysis that used to take about four hours could now be done in around 10 minutes, with no real particles missed along the way.

sentences.en: The result of swapping blind digging for this smarter search was dramatic: An analysis that used to take about four hours could now be done in around 10 minutes, with no real particles missed along the way.
sentences.zh: 将盲目挖掘改为这种更智能的搜索的结果是戏剧性的：过去需要大约四个小时的分析现在可以在大约 10 分钟内完成，并且一路上不会遗漏任何真正的粒子。

blocks.html_en: Batra explains, "Not every data point is equally informative for training a machine learning model. Active learning addresses this by selecting a small but highly informative subset of data, enabling the model to learn more efficiently."

sentences.en: Batra explains, "Not every data point is equally informative for training a machine learning model.
sentences.zh: Batra 解释说：“对于训练机器学习模型来说，并不是每个数据点都具有同等的信息量。

sentences.en: Active learning addresses this by selecting a small but highly informative subset of data, enabling the model to learn more efficiently."
sentences.zh: 主动学习通过选择一个小但信息丰富的数据子集来解决这个问题，使模型能够更有效地学习。”

sentences.en: Three possible family trees

blocks.html_en: With the search done, the team had a clear map, and it turned out the family of three Higgs bosons can be arranged in three different ways, depending on whether the 125 GeV Higgs we already know is the youngest, middle or oldest sibling.

sentences.en: With the search done, the team had a clear map, and it turned out the family of three Higgs bosons can be arranged in three different ways, depending on whether the 125 GeV Higgs we already know is the youngest, middle or oldest sibling.
sentences.zh: 搜索完成后，团队有了清晰的地图，结果发现三个希格斯玻色子家族可以以三种不同的方式排列，具体取决于我们已知的 125 GeV 希格斯玻色子是最年轻的、中间的还是最年长的兄弟姐妹。

blocks.html_en: In the first arrangement, our known Higgs is the youngest, the lightest of the three. Here, the model is well-behaved. Its two heavier siblings are predicted to weigh somewhere between roughly 350 and 580 GeV, several times heavier than the Higgs we have already found.

sentences.en: In the first arrangement, our known Higgs is the youngest, the lightest of the three.
sentences.zh: 在第一种排列中，我们已知的希格斯粒子是三者中最年轻、最轻的。

sentences.en: Here, the model is well-behaved.
sentences.zh: 在这里，模型表现良好。

sentences.en: Its two heavier siblings are predicted to weigh somewhere between roughly 350 and 580 GeV, several times heavier than the Higgs we have already found.
sentences.zh: 它的两个较重的兄弟姐妹预计重量约为 350 至 580 GeV，比我们已经发现的希格斯粒子重几倍。

blocks.html_en: Nature, it seems, is allowed to have bigger siblings hiding just out of reach of past experiments, but not absolutely any weight will do; they have to fall inside this specific window.

sentences.en: Nature, it seems, is allowed to have bigger siblings hiding just out of reach of past experiments, but not absolutely any weight will do; they have to fall inside this specific window.
sentences.zh: 大自然似乎允许将更大的兄弟姐妹隐藏在过去实验无法触及的地方，但绝对不是任何重量都可以；他们必须落入这个特定的窗口内。

blocks.html_en: The most interesting twist comes from the second arrangement, where our known Higgs is the middle child. This setup quietly allows for something remarkable: a second, lighter Higgs boson, possibly as light as 82 GeV, that nobody has detected yet.

sentences.en: The most interesting twist comes from the second arrangement, where our known Higgs is the middle child.
sentences.zh: 最有趣的转折来自第二种安排，我们已知的希格斯粒子是中间的孩子。

sentences.en: This setup quietly allows for something remarkable: a second, lighter Higgs boson, possibly as light as 82 GeV, that nobody has detected yet.
sentences.zh: 这种设置悄悄地允许了一些非凡的事情：第二个更轻的希格斯玻色子，可能轻至 82 GeV，目前还没有人检测到。

blocks.html_en: It is not that this particle would have been invisible; it is that it may interact with other particles differently enough to have hidden in plain sight within data we already have. That is the headline result of the whole study. A sibling of the Higgs boson, lighter than the one history books already credited with completing the Standard Model, remains entirely on the table.

sentences.en: It is not that this particle would have been invisible; it is that it may interact with other particles differently enough to have hidden in plain sight within data we already have.

sentences.en: That is the headline result of the whole study.

sentences.en: A sibling of the Higgs boson, lighter than the one history books already credited with completing the Standard Model, remains entirely on the table.

sentences.en: The third arrangement is the one nature seems to veto.

content_html_zh:
如果 2012 年发现的希格斯玻色子并不孤单，而且是我们迄今为止遇到的唯一的兄弟，该怎么办？ 欧洲核子研究组织的科学家当年发现了这种粒子，这是一项重大发现，因为它解释了其他粒子如何获得质量。 长期以来，科学家们认为这是谜题的最后一块。

他们有一个称为标准模型的框架，该框架描述了我们所看到的一切中最小的粒子。 这包括原子中的电子和称为光子的光粒子。 然而，这个框架并不能解释一切。 它没有告诉我们暗物质，也没有告诉我们为什么宇宙的物质比反物质多得多。 这就像一张地图只显示了世界的一半。

希格斯玻色子的发现提出了新的问题。 许多物理学家开始怀疑我们发现的希格斯粒子是否是唯一的一种。 他们开始询问宇宙中是否隐藏着更大的这些粒子家族。 如果我们找到这个家族的更多成员，我们可能最终会理解当前框架所遗漏的自然部分。

三希格斯玻色子提议

这个想法是印度理工学院甘地讷格尔研究人员最近两项研究的焦点。 他们与 Harish-Chandra 研究所 (HRI) 的专家合作，探索了一种理论，其中这些领域存在三种类型，而不仅仅是一种。

印度理工学院甘地讷格尔分校的团队成员包括拥有博士学位的 Akshat Khanna。 物理学； Baradhwaj Coleppa，物理学副教授； Nipun Batra，计算机科学与工程副教授；和戈库尔 B. 克里希纳（Krishna）拥有博士学位。 在物理学中。 他们在杜伦大学举行的 PASCOS 国际会议上发表了他们的发现并分享了他们的工作。

他们的第一项研究发表在《Physical Review D》上，使用了一种称为主动学习的机器学习方法，对数千种可能性进行了排序，奠定了基础。

第二项研究发表在《欧洲物理杂志》上，研究了未来的粒子对撞机如何检测这些新的家庭成员。 这些论文共同为未来的科学实验提供了更好的地图。

各领域如何分工

要理解他们的工作，请将希格斯场视为宇宙的基本组成部分。 在标准框架中，只有这些块之一。 随着宇宙的演化，与这个场的相互作用为构成我们周围一切的所有粒子提供了质量。 这留下了一个希格斯粒子。

新理论表明存在三种不同的构建模块。 这意味着将会出现几种新型粒子。 有些可能带有电荷，而另一些可能会以我们以前从未见过的方式表现。

每个块还带有一个背景值——即使在空白空间中的场强度——并且，用三个块而不是一个，场可以彼此混合。 其结果是希格斯粒子的集合更加丰富，包括标准模型中不存在的带电希格斯玻色子，现在正在实验中寻找。

这种特定的模型通常被称为民主理论，因为这三个构建模块共同承担为不同种类的物质提供质量的工作。 其中一个模块负责处理电子等粒子。 另一个块处理一组特定的夸克，第三个块处理另一组夸克。

如果这些构建块都与相同种类的物质自由相互作用，它们可能会引起实验中从未见过的奇怪反应。 通过为每个块分配特定的工作，该理论与我们已知的事实保持一致。

将已知的希格斯粒子拟合进去

这项研究中的一个重要想法是确定哪些新粒子是我们已经发现的粒子。 由于我们知道当前希格斯玻色子的质量，因此我们必须将其放入新的家族中。 它可以是最轻的构件，也可以是中间的构件。

它甚至可能是最重的成员。 这些不同的安排改变了家庭其他成员的外观。 研究人员根据最新的科学数据对这些场景进行了研究，看看哪些场景最有意义。

模型中的每组参数都必须经过多次严格的测试才被认为有效。 系统的能量必须保持稳定，这样才不会崩溃。 这些预测还必须与过去粒子对撞机实验的数据相匹配。

最重要的是，我们已经发现的希格斯粒子的外观和行为必须仍然与我们观察到的相同。 新粒子不会干扰我们已经证明是正确的物理定律。 这使得理论立足于现实。

Coleppa 解释说：“仍有大量理论可能性可以使该模型与实验观察结果保持一致。 我们的任务是以最普遍、最全面的方式测试这些可能性。”

教导搜索在哪里挖掘

这就是问题的规模变得近乎滑稽的地方。 想象一下有 14 个不同转盘的棋盘游戏，每个转盘都有不同的设置。 只需打开或关闭一个拨盘，您就已经拥有 214 种或超过 16,000 种组合。

但这些转盘并不是简单的开关；它们是一个简单的开关。每个都可以设置为一定范围内的任何值，就像音量旋钮而不是灯开关。 为了正确地设计这个游戏，团队生成了 6000 亿个质量和角度设置的随机组合，并根据规则测试了每一个组合。

在这 6000 亿次尝试中，只有一小部分能够通过所有测试。 用传统方法一次检查每一项，就像在银行金库中手工尝试每一种可能的组合一样。

将整个 14 转盘搜索空间想象成一片广阔、雾气弥漫的海滩，沙子里埋着一些重要的硬币。 到处发出蜂鸣声的金属探测器是没有用的；你会永远挖下去。 研究人员使用的技巧称为主动学习，更接近于从已经挖掘的位置进行学习的更智能的探测器。 它从小处开始，挖掘一些随机点并跟踪哪些点出现了硬币。

几轮后，它完全停止随机挖掘。 它开始注意到沙子上有一条粗糙的线：一侧，硬币不断出现；另一侧，硬币不断出现；另一侧，硬币不断出现。另一方面，什么也没有。 沿着这条线就是它不断令人惊讶的地方。

因此，这就是它下一步挖掘的地方，一次又一次，每个新洞都会增强它对这条线的确切位置的感觉，直到它在不触及大部分海滩的情况下拥有整个边界的自信地图。 作为最后的安全检查，任何被标记为有希望的东西都会被手工挖掘出来，只是为了确保这不是一场虚惊。

将盲目挖掘改为这种更智能的搜索的结果是戏剧性的：过去需要大约四个小时的分析现在可以在大约 10 分钟内完成，并且一路上不会遗漏任何真正的粒子。

Batra 解释说：“对于训练机器学习模型来说，并不是每个数据点都具有同等的信息量。 主动学习通过选择一个小但信息丰富的数据子集来解决这个问题，使模型能够更有效地学习。”

三种可能的家谱

搜索完成后，团队有了清晰的地图，结果发现三个希格斯玻色子家族可以以三种不同的方式排列，具体取决于我们已知的 125 GeV 希格斯玻色子是最年轻的、中间的还是最年长的兄弟姐妹。

在第一种排列中，我们已知的希格斯粒子是三者中最年轻、最轻的。 在这里，模型表现良好。 它的两个较重的兄弟姐妹预计重量约为 350 至 580 GeV，比我们已经发现的希格斯粒子重几倍。

大自然似乎允许将更大的兄弟姐妹隐藏在过去实验无法触及的地方，但绝对不是任何重量都可以；他们必须落入这个特定的窗口内。

最有趣的转折来自第二种安排，我们已知的希格斯粒子是中间的孩子。 这种设置悄悄地允许了一些非凡的事情：第二个更轻的希格斯玻色子，可能轻至 82 GeV，目前还没有人检测到。

这并不是说这个粒子是不可见的；而是说它是可见的。它与其他粒子的相互作用可能不同，足以隐藏在我们已有的数据中。 这是整个研究的主要结果。 希格斯玻色子的一个兄弟，比已经被认为完成了标准模型的那本历史书要轻，仍然完全留在桌面上。

第三种安排是大自然似乎否决的一种安排。 在这里，我们已知的希格斯玻色子必须是这三种玻色子中最古老、最重的，这意味着有两个尚未发现的轻于 125 GeV 的希格斯玻色子漂浮在周围。 从表面上看，这听起来和中间孩子的案例一样令人兴奋。 但当团队通过全面的测试来推动这个场景时，它失败了。

狩猎用的清洁机器

第二篇论文着眼于我们如何真正找到这些隐藏的粒子。 研究人员重点研究了一种名为国际直线对撞机的拟议机器。 这台机器会碰撞微小的颗粒，创造一个非常干净的研究环境。 它与我们今天使用的机器不同，因为它可以让科学家更清楚地看到碰撞的结果。

研究小组研究了这台未来机器在实验室环境中产生新希格斯家族成员的几种方法。

研究人员发现了几种有希望的方法来发现新粒子。 当机器碰撞粒子时，它可以产生一对新的希格斯粒子家族。 这些粒子很快分解成我们可以看到和测量的其他东西。 通过计算这些最终的碎片，科学家可以将真实信号与背景噪声分开。

这类似于在拥挤的房间里聆听特定的声音。 如果您知道要听什么，即使有很多其他声音，您也可以找到所需的信息。

研究表明，其中许多途径可以带来真正的发现。 如果机器运行一定时间，某些通道很可能会显示结果。 研究人员研究了不同类型的信号，包括产生特定夸克和轻子模式的信号。

这为未来的实验提供了一套清晰的说明。 它将理论图变成了建造和运行这些大型机器的科学家的实用指南。

从理论到测试计划

这项工作的优点在于它将理论与实验联系起来。 第一项研究使用智能计算机来寻找最佳可能性，第二项研究告诉我们如何寻找它们。 这非常重要，因为有太多选择的理论可能很难检验。

印度理工学院甘地讷格尔分校的研究人员通过缩小搜索范围，使他们的理论变得可检验。 正如该团队所解释的那样，将物理学与智能计算机策略相结合使我们能够比以前更快地寻找宇宙的秘密。

这项研究不仅仅涉及一种理论。 它有助于全球努力了解希格斯玻色子是单独存在还是有兄弟姐妹。 它还证明智能计算机工具可以帮助科学家解决非常复杂的问题。

这种方法可以用于许多其他科学领域，这些领域有太多的可能性需要测试。 近期目标是帮助寻找新粒子，但长期目标是改善我们在信息如此丰​​富的世界中进行科学研究的方式。

希格斯玻色子的故事实际上是一个关于宇宙如何构建的故事。 我们从一个粒子开始，但我们可能有一个更大的家庭。 印度理工学院甘地讷格尔分校的研究表明，这个想法非常有活力。

一个较轻的兄弟姐妹可能隐藏在我们当前的数据中，而其他兄弟姐妹可能正在等待未来的机器。 通过使用智能计算机绘制地图和对撞机研究来引导，我们越来越接近了解世界的完整架构。

卡纳补充道：“我们工作的关键是使用创新方法，例如将现代机器学习技术与粒子物理学相结合来应对艰巨的挑战。 在不久的将来，我渴望进一步开展这一研究，寻找新粒子的证据。”
